analysis: The mixed hard/uniform-negative trial completed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 to 0.4838, versus 0.5025 for the preceding uniform-negative model and the historical best of 0.5375. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.520, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.535, Electronics 0.380, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.500. Electronics fell from 0.395 to 0.380. These results do not support this negative-mining configuration. Selecting high-scoring negatives may overemphasize false negatives or distort the training objective relative to uniformly sampled evaluation candidates, but this trial does not establish the cause. It consumed 1,136.99 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Retained per-dataset SASRec with 64-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, item biases, and a gated preference branch using an exponential prefix mean with a ten-interaction half-life. Changed training to sample 144 negatives with replacement, excluding complete training histories: 128 mining candidates plus 16 independent uniform competitors. At each valid position, detached scores select the top 16 mining candidates; their logits are recomputed with gradients and combined with the uniform competitors and positive in 33-way cross-entropy. Preserved twenty-target temporal weighting and equal weight per nonempty sequence. Inference architecture, four-category routing, strict checkpoint loading, and predictor generation remained aligned.
